skill.description: Create AI avatar, talking-head, and lip-sync videos with RunComfy. The skill selects the right avatar model, prepares the RunComfy CLI call, and gives model-specific prompting guidance for portraits, scripts, and audio tracks.
skill.summary: Create talking-head and lip-sync avatar videos with RunComfy model routing.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, example URLs, documentation links, and explanatory token-storage text. No prompt injection attempt, covert credential exfiltration, or direct hidden-file access instruction was found. The real risks are intentional RunComfy media upload and dual-use synthetic avatar generation.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before sending portraits, audio, prompts, or references to RunComfy endpoints.
Keep refusal rules for real people without consent, and ask users to confirm rights before generation.
Keep autonomous tool use limited to runcomfy commands, and make install, login, and token setup user-confirmed steps.
Consider moving installation examples to prose or setup documentation to reduce markdown backtick false positives.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration and How it works section clearly describe networked RunComfy CLI behavior. The risk is transparent and intentional, not covert.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar Talking Head Videos
content.value_statement: Avatar video work often requires choosing between several model workflows. This skill routes the request and prepares the correct RunComfy generation path.
actual_capabilities: Routes avatar video requests to OmniHuman, Wan, HappyHorse, Seedance, or Wan Animate.
Prepares RunComfy CLI inputs for portrait plus audio, script-only, or cinematic reference workflows.
Explains when to use audio_url, reference audio, or quoted speech inside the prompt.
Links users to relevant RunComfy model pages and CLI documentation.
Provides consent and safety guidance for likeness and voice use.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Uploads user prompts, portraits, audio, and references to RunComfy services.
Cannot verify that a user has rights to a person's likeness or voice.
Output quality depends on source media, selected model, and current model availability.

use_cases.title: Produce UGC-Style Product Clips
use_cases.description: Create a short presenter video from a portrait and approved voiceover for ads or product launches.

use_cases.title: Create Training Presenters
use_cases.description: Turn a prepared script or audio lesson into a talking-head training clip for internal education.

use_cases.title: Prototype Localized Demo Videos
use_cases.description: Reuse an approved presenter image with different audio tracks for language variants and product demos.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Talking Head
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one portrait and one voiceover.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head avatar video from this portrait and voiceover. Use the simplest RunComfy model that fits.

prompt_templates.title: Script Without Audio
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a script but no recorded voice file.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this short script but no audio file. Choose a RunComfy path that can generate speech and video together.

prompt_templates.title: Stylized Character Sync
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a mascot or illustrated character to speak.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this stylized character with the provided voiceover. Pick the model best suited for non-photoreal subjects.

prompt_templates.title: Cinematic Reference Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with subject, scene, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cinematic avatar monologue using this subject reference, scene direction, and approved audio track.

output_examples.input: A user provides a portrait and an approved voiceover for a vertical product ad.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends OmniHuman, explains why it fits, and gives a concise RunComfy execution plan.

output_examples.input: A user has a written presenter script but no audio file.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends HappyHorse, explains how to quote the spoken line, and notes expected speech limits.

output_examples.input: A user wants a cinematic monologue with subject and audio references.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Seedance v2 Pro and describes how to match references, lens direction, and duration.

best_practices: Confirm rights to the portrait, voice, and script before generating a person-like video.
Use clean voiceover audio without music when precise lip sync matters.
Pick the smallest model route that satisfies the scene, audio, and character requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not create videos of real people without clear consent for likeness and voice use.
Do not use script-only workflows when exact timing or exact audio identity is required.
Do not upload private media unless the user approves RunComfy processing.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create avatar videos, talking-head clips, lip-sync scenes, and virtual presenter videos through RunComfy.

faq.question: Does it need a recorded audio file?
faq.answer: Some routes need audio. HappyHorse can create speech from a written prompt when no audio file exists.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and sends generation requests to RunComfy services.

faq.question: Can it make a real person speak?
faq.answer: Only with proper rights and consent for both the person's likeness and the speaker's voice.

faq.question: What should I prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare an approved portrait or character image, clean audio or a short script, and the desired video format.
